# m6 contact sheet
# Part 4 of 5 (m6-contact-sheet-1.txt … m6-contact-sheet-5.txt), each at most 180 000 B.
#
# Promise: a real conflict is resolvable without leaving the app — each shape a merge, rebase or stash pop stops on is taken, staged and continued by keys, and the bytes are what the command line's own checkout gives (TESTING.md "Conflicts walk", "Conflict journeys").
#
# Generated by scripts/contact-sheet.sh — do not hand-edit; edit
# m6-contact-sheet-captions.tsv and re-run instead.
#
# 181 captures in all, in ticket order.
#
# These are character-grid captures (pyte/TestBackend), not pixels:
# colour is never verifiable from this file. Judge colour only in a
# real terminal, never from a capture (CLAUDE.md rule 5).
#
# Scroll once: each capture is delimited by a heading naming its
# file (docs/shots/<name>) and what right looks like for it.

# TestBackend capture (not a pty), 80x24, no colour recorded. Fixture:
# capture_fix_box_owns_the_bar in crates/graft/tests/it/box_owns_the_bar.rs
# (asserted). Four frames, each a box open over a status that was standing.
#
# What right looks like, the bottom row of each frame:
# 1. A teammate pushed; `P` `→` `⏎` was rejected, then `P` opened the lease
#    box: `←/→ move  ⏎ choose  esc cancel` — the box's keys, not the
#    rejection line (which named `p`, a key the box swallows).
# 2. `esc` on that box: the rejection is back, `push rejected: … · p pull
#    first · P force with lease` — hidden under the box, never cleared.
# 3. Another repository: a checkout, an edit, then `u` over the drift box:
#    `y undo  ←/→ move  ⏎ choose  esc cancel` — not `undo · esc cancels`,
#    the finished job's busy line.
# 4. Back on the first: `b`, then `⏎` on the empty name: the prompt stays
#    open, and the row reads `a branch needs a name` — the prompt's own
#    refusal, written to the prompt, not the status line.
# - Colour is unverified (CLAUDE.md rule 5).
#

docs/shots/m6/fix-undo-drift-way-back-120x40.txt
what right looks like: (ticket 77; frames 1 and 4 by ticket 80) The edit an undo replaces, and the way back. Frame 1: a menu checkout of `fix`, `fix.txt` edited, the graph settled (no `sorting…`), `u`: under what moved, the box reads `Undo replaces your edit to fix.txt; a backup keeps it, and U brings it back.`, whole. Frame 2: `y`: no changes row, and the bottom row `undo: checkout fix ✓ · U brings back your edit to fix.txt`; the graph marks `[◆ main]` and `fix` plain, as git's HEAD is `main`, with the Radar's `ⓘ` on `fix` (ticket 79: an undo that moves HEAD re-reads the graph). Frame 3: `U`: the changes row is back, `(1 unstaged)`, and `redo: checkout fix ✓`; the edit's bytes are asserted from the file. Frame 4: a second repository, the journal's time machine run back to before `checkout fix` past its drift box: the bottom row `reverted to before “checkout fix” (2 steps) ✓ · U (2 times) brings it back` — the path dropped so the key fits 80 columns. Colour unverified.
================================================================================

# TestBackend capture (not a pty), 120x40, no colour recorded. Fixture:
# capture_fix_undo_drift_way_back in crates/graft/tests/it/undo_over_drift.rs
# (asserted). m6-conflicts/77: a menu checkout of `fix`, `fix.txt` edited,
# then `u`, `y`, `U`.
#
# What right looks like:
# 1. The drift box: under what moved, `Undo replaces your edit to fix.txt;
#    a backup keeps it, and U brings it back.` — whole, not cut. The graph
#    under it has settled: no `sorting…` (asserted; m6-conflicts/80).
# 2. After `y`: no changes row, and the bottom row reads `undo: checkout
#    fix ✓ · U brings back your edit to fix.txt`. `HEAD` is on `main` in
#    git and the graph marks `[◆ main]`, `fix` plain (both asserted;
#    m6-conflicts/79). The Radar has answered: its `ⓘ` is on `fix`.
# 3. After `U`: the changes row is back, `(1 unstaged)`, and `redo:
#    checkout fix ✓`. `HEAD` is on `fix` again and the edit's bytes are
#    back (both asserted from git and the file, not the frame).
# 4. A second repository: `fix`, then `fix2`, checked out, `fix.txt`
#    edited, and the journal's time machine run back to before `checkout
#    fix` past its drift box. The bottom row reads `reverted to before
#    “checkout fix” (2 steps) ✓ · U (2 times) brings it back`, whole at 80
#    columns: the path is dropped before the key (asserted; m6-conflicts/80).
# - Colour is unverified (CLAUDE.md rule 5).
#

docs/shots/m6/fix-status-under-a-box-120x40.txt
what right looks like: (ticket 78) A status that arrives under a box is held, and the name prompt refuses a second write inside itself. The bottom row of each frame: 1. `f` to a remote that is not there, `b`, the fetch fails under the prompt: `⏎ create  ⇥ toggle  esc cancel`, the prompt's keys. 2. `topic ⏎`: the held failure, `fetch all remotes failed: … · esc dismiss`. 3. `esc`: `branch topic at …`, the create's line; the create was not cancelled. 4. `f`, `b`, `other ⏎` while that fetch runs: `wait for fetch all remotes to finish`, the prompt still open with `other` kept. 5. The fetch answers: the prompt's keys again. 6. `esc`: `fetched ✓`. Colour unverified.
================================================================================

# TestBackend capture (not a pty), 120x40, no colour recorded. Fixture:
# capture_fix_status_under_a_box in crates/graft/tests/it/status_under_a_box.rs
# (asserted). Six frames, one sitting: a fetch fails under the name prompt,
# then a second fetch runs while the prompt is up again.
#
# What right looks like, the bottom row of each frame:
# 1. `f` (to a remote that is not there), `b`, and the fetch fails while the
#    prompt is up: the prompt's keys — the failure is held, not drawn over
#    the box and not lost.
# 2. `topic ⏎`: the prompt closes and the row is the held fetch failure,
#    `… · esc dismiss` — not the create's busy line, which would hide it.
# 3. `esc`: the failure dismissed, the create's own line. The create is not
#    cancelled: `esc` dismissed a drawn failure first.
# 4. `f` again (the remote back), `b`, `other ⏎` while that fetch runs: the
#    prompt stays open with `other` kept, and the row reads `wait for fetch …
#    to finish` — refused inside the prompt, no second write started.
# 5. The fetch answers: the row is the prompt's keys again (the refusal went
#    with its cause); one `⏎` would now create.
# 6. `esc`: the prompt closes and the fetch's finished line shows, with its
#    tick — it arrived under the box and was not acknowledged unseen.
# - Colour is unverified (CLAUDE.md rule 5).
#
=== frame 1: `f` to nowhere, `b`, the fetch fails under the prompt ===

docs/shots/m6/fix-status-under-a-box-80x24.txt
what right looks like: (ticket 78) The same six frames at 80x24: the same six bottom rows, whole.
================================================================================

# TestBackend capture (not a pty), 80x24, no colour recorded. Fixture:
# capture_fix_status_under_a_box in crates/graft/tests/it/status_under_a_box.rs
# (asserted). Six frames, one sitting: a fetch fails under the name prompt,
# then a second fetch runs while the prompt is up again.
#
# What right looks like, the bottom row of each frame:
# 1. `f` (to a remote that is not there), `b`, and the fetch fails while the
#    prompt is up: the prompt's keys — the failure is held, not drawn over
#    the box and not lost.
# 2. `topic ⏎`: the prompt closes and the row is the held fetch failure,
#    `… · esc dismiss` — not the create's busy line, which would hide it.
# 3. `esc`: the failure dismissed, the create's own line. The create is not
#    cancelled: `esc` dismissed a drawn failure first.
# 4. `f` again (the remote back), `b`, `other ⏎` while that fetch runs: the
#    prompt stays open with `other` kept, and the row reads `wait for fetch …
#    to finish` — refused inside the prompt, no second write started.
# 5. The fetch answers: the row is the prompt's keys again (the refusal went
#    with its cause); one `⏎` would now create.
# 6. `esc`: the prompt closes and the fetch's finished line shows, with its
#    tick — it arrived under the box and was not acknowledged unseen.
# - Colour is unverified (CLAUDE.md rule 5).
#

docs/shots/m6/fix-tab-words-120x40.txt
what right looks like: (ticket 70) Every `⇥` word names where `⇥` lands. Frame 1: a rebase stop, the changes pane's files focused: the bar ends `⇥ diff`, not `⇥ graph`. Frame 2: `a`: the bottom row reads `rebase in progress · ⇥ ⇥ banner, then c continue  a abort`, two tabs, as the cycle takes. Frames 3-4: one `⇥` (the diff), then a second (the banner has the keyboard); the refusal is sticky and still stands, counted from the files (an open question in the ticket). Frame 5: a merge begun in the shell, the banner focused: its bar says `c finish`, not `c continue`. Frame 6: an untracked `new.txt`: its row reads `new`, not `bin`; the body shows its content as added lines, `1 + hello from new` (ticket 81). Colour unverified.
================================================================================
